name: Hotel Ritz Paris
insider_take: The epitome of Parisian luxury since 1898, where Coco Chanel lived for 34 years and Hemingway personally "liberated" the bar in 1944.
whats_special: This legendary palace hotel on Place Vendôme features the world's first hotel cooking school, L'Ecole Ritz Escoffier, and houses one of the largest wine cellars in Paris with over 25,000 bottles. The Imperial Suite was Coco Chanel's actual residence, complete with her original furnishings and secret passages she used to access her boutique.
pro_tip: Book afternoon tea at Salon Proust - it's served in the exact salon where Marcel Proust wrote parts of "In Search of Lost Time," and the madeleines are made using his era's original recipe.
dont_miss: The Bar Hemingway, where Colin Field has been crafting legendary cocktails for decades, and the Ritz Club Paris - the city's most exclusive underground spa and fitness club featuring the hotel's stunning indoor pool beneath crystal chandeliers.
pros: Iconic palace hotel with legendary Parisian elegance and history
Prime location on Place Vendôme near luxury shopping and major attractions
World-renowned Ritz Paris Escoffier cooking school on-site
Exceptional fine dining including Michelin-starred L'Espadon restaurant
Lavish spa and wellness facilities with indoor swimming pool
cons: Ultra-luxury pricing reflects palace hotel status
Formal atmosphere may not suit all travelers
